eventStaff.intro: Give hosts, crew and outdoor teams a shared event identity with clothing suited to each role. With 20 years of clothing experience, LF adapts existing styles or develops new garments, managing samples and production follow-up around your event requirements.

outfitPlan.note: These are planning examples. Choose individual items or combine them around your own event roles.

sections.heading: One event identity, clothing for each role.
sections.body: Shared colours and artwork connect different staff outfits. Use the sample to check whether a logo remains visible under a jacket and whether role identification is clear. Specify size quantities for each garment and include any spare clothing needed on site.

Separate size quantities by item, including any spare clothing you need.

sections.heading: Turn your event look into clothing people can wear.
sections.body: A reference photo, AI concept, sketch or existing garment is enough to begin; a finished tech pack is not required. LF develops the fabric, fit, construction and branding details for sampling. Check movement, pockets and appearance before production. Semi-custom and fully developed garments follow the same quality requirements set for your order.
items: Show the details you want to keep and those you want to change.
Check artwork size and position on each garment type.
Approve the sample, materials and order details before bulk production.

sections.heading: Plan from the date your team needs the clothing.
sections.body: Share the arrival date and destination, allowing time to distribute clothing before the event. Sampling, feedback, material readiness, production and shipping all shape the schedule. Specialist production partners make the garments; LF manages development, samples, production follow-up, quality checks and packing. Include crew groups and carton markings in the brief so clothing can be prepared for your distribution plan.

faqs.question: Should we customise an existing style or develop a new one?
faqs.answer: If an existing style gives your team the fit and appearance it needs, start with colours, logos or selected detail changes. For a different fabric, silhouette or construction, discuss full development. We explain the work involved and quote for your chosen route.

faqs.question: What is the minimum order for event clothing, and what do you need to quote?
faqs.answer: The usual minimum order for regular event clothing is 50 garments per style/colour. Send references, quantities by garment, size requirements, artwork, destination and the date staff need their clothing. A simple list is enough to begin, and we will help fill in the garment details needed for a quotation.

faqs.question: When does sampling start, and how is the event schedule set?
faqs.answer: After order confirmation and payment of the sample fee, sampling starts as soon as possible. Clothing samples take 7–12 days. Bulk timing depends on your products, quantities, materials and customisation. We plan production and shipping separately around approvals and your required arrival date before agreeing the schedule. For orders of 100 pieces or more, the sample fee can be credited against the bulk order payment.

faqs.question: Can we request fabric reports or garment testing?
faqs.answer: Yes. We can arrange fabric and finished-garment testing and provide the resulting reports. Tell us which tests your purchasing team needs. Testing of custom finished garments carries an additional fee, with scope and cost set out beforehand. Reports apply to what was tested; a fabric report does not by itself certify the finished garment.

faqs.question: Can we reorder clothing for another event?
faqs.answer: Yes. We keep one garment from each bulk order as a physical reference for repeat orders. Send your previous order reference, new quantities and any branding changes. The retained garment helps us compare fit, construction and finish; materials, trims and the new schedule are checked for the repeat order.

corporate.intro: Bring suits, polos, workwear and related items into one staff clothing plan, with coordinated branding across departments. LF brings 20 years of clothing experience and manages development, samples and production follow-up, whether you are updating familiar uniforms or creating a new company look.

sections.body: Specialist production partners make the garments, while LF manages specifications, samples, production follow-up, quality checks and packing. We communicate progress and issues through one contact. Include site requirements and staff distribution plans early so size breakdowns, packing instructions and delivery dates can be coordinated across the range.

faqs.question: Should we update existing uniforms or develop new garments?
faqs.answer: If the current style works well, start with branding, colours or selected detail changes. Full development suits a brief that calls for a different fabric, fit or construction. Both routes follow your quality requirements. We explain the materials, quantities and development costs in your quotation.

faqs.question: What is the minimum order for regular staff clothing?
faqs.answer: The usual minimum is 50 garments per style/colour for regular clothing orders. Send the quantities needed for each item and staff group so we can plan the range and prepare the quotation. Footwear, towels, PPE and other related products have their own ordering requirements, which we discuss for the items you select.

faqs.question: Can we start with pictures instead of a technical pack?
faqs.answer: Yes. Reference photos, an AI concept, a sketch or an existing garment are enough to begin. Show what you like and what needs to change. We help develop the practical specification for sampling, including fabric, measurements, garment details and branding.

faqs.question: When does sampling start, and how long does an order take?
faqs.answer: After order confirmation and payment of the sample fee, we start sampling as soon as possible. Clothing samples take 7–12 days. Bulk timing depends on each product, quantity and customisation, including approvals and material readiness. We set out the item schedules and shipping separately against your required arrival dates. For orders of 100 pieces or more, the sample fee can be credited against the bulk order payment.

faqs.question: Can our purchasing team request test reports?
faqs.answer: Yes. We can arrange fabric and finished-garment testing and provide reports for your purchasing team. Tests on custom finished garments carry an additional fee, with scope and cost set out beforehand. Tell us the tests or standards you need; PPE and other protective items require evidence for the particular product and intended use.

faqs.question: How do you help keep repeat staff orders consistent?
faqs.answer: We retain one garment from each bulk order to help align future orders with the original production. It provides a reference for fit, construction and branding when you need clothing for additional staff or departments. Material and trim availability is checked again before a repeat order is arranged.

workwear.title: Custom Workwear Manufacturer in China | LF Clothing
workwear.description: Custom workwear for company teams. LF manages development and sampling, with production organised through specialist manufacturing partners in China.
workwear.heading: Custom workwear built around your team’s daily work.
workwear.intro: Plan jackets, work trousers and coveralls around daily tasks, with consistent company branding. With 20 years of clothing experience, LF helps adapt familiar workwear or develop new designs, managing garment development, samples and production follow-up through one supplier contact.

orderSummary.label: Clothing samples
orderSummary.value: Usually 7–12 days. Sampling starts after order confirmation and payment of the sample fee.

orderSummary.label: Sample fee credit
orderSummary.value: For orders of 100 pieces or more, the sample fee can be credited against the bulk order payment.

orderSummary.label: Repeat-order reference
orderSummary.value: One garment retained from each bulk order to help align future orders.

sections.heading: Start with how your team works.
sections.body: Tell us what staff carry, how they move and where clothing gets the most wear. For trousers, consider the waistband, rise, leg shape and closures. Jackets and coveralls need room for reach and layers. Include washing conditions and reinforcement needs when choosing fabric, pockets and construction.
items: Place pockets around the tools and everyday items staff need to carry.
Describe working positions and any layers.
Share fabric preferences, washing requirements and areas that need attention.

sections.heading: Keep what works and improve the details.
sections.body: Bring a current garment and mark what staff want to keep or change. Retain its fit while adjusting colour, branding or details, or develop different materials and construction. A photo, sketch or AI concept can also start the specification and sample. Both routes follow your quality requirements; assess fit, pocket access and appearance before production.

sections.heading: Keep production connected to the approved sample.
sections.body: Specialist production partners make the garments; LF manages development, samples and production follow-up. The approved sample guides checks on measurements, materials, seams, closures, logos, quantities and packing. Fabric and finished-garment testing can be arranged with reports for the tests performed. Custom finished-garment tests cost extra, so include testing needs in the initial brief.

sections.heading: Plan the order by garment and staff group.
sections.body: List jackets and trousers separately, even when they form a set, with size quantities for each staff group. Add artwork, destinations and required arrival dates, plus any team or location labels needed for packing. Materials, quantities and customisation shape the quotation.

faqs.question: Do we need full development for a conventional workwear order?
faqs.answer: No. If a familiar style already fits the job, start with logo application and selected colour or detail changes. For a different fabric, fit, pocket layout or construction, discuss the development needed. We explain the options and cost from your reference and quantities; a new design is not required for every order.

faqs.question: What is the minimum quantity for workwear or specialist garments?
faqs.answer: The usual minimum for regular workwear is 50 garments per style/colour. Specialist, complex clothing projects, such as flight suits or racing suits, may be possible from 10 garments after review of the design, materials and production requirements. This lower quantity is assessed for the specialist project, rather than applied to ordinary workwear or event clothing.

faqs.question: Can different departments wear different garments with the same branding?
faqs.answer: Yes. Shared artwork and colour references can connect jackets, trousers, coveralls and other staff clothing across your teams. Each garment can retain the details needed for its role. Send the staff groups and garment quantities together so we can plan the range and samples as one order.

faqs.question: When do sampling and bulk production begin?
faqs.answer: After order confirmation and payment of the sample fee, sampling starts as soon as possible. Clothing samples take 7–12 days. Bulk production follows approval of the sample, materials and order details. Timing depends on the products, quantities and customisation; production and shipping are planned against your required arrival date. For orders of 100 pieces or more, the sample fee can be credited against the bulk order payment.

faqs.question: What if our workwear needs protective performance?
faqs.answer: Share the intended use, destination market and required standards at the start. We assess the garment, materials and testing needed for those requirements. Any custom garment tests are quoted separately. The finished garment needs its own supporting evidence; a fabric report alone does not establish certification.

faqs.question: What reference do you keep for a repeat workwear order?
faqs.answer: LF keeps one garment from each bulk order. For a repeat order, it helps us compare the fit, pockets, construction and branding with the previous production. Send the earlier order reference and any changes you need. We check material and trim availability before setting up the new order.
